p.seg: Chapter One: On the Heavenly Purity of High Antiquity
1.1 Once upon a time, the Yellow Emperor (Huángdì)
was born with spiritual intelligence.
While weak, he could speak;
as a child, he was quick and discerning;
as he grew, he was earnest and perceptive;
upon maturity, he ascended to heaven.
Thereupon, he asked the Heavenly Teacher (Tiān Shī), saying:
"I have heard that
the people of high antiquity
all lived past one hundred years
and their movements did not decline.
The people of today,
halfway to one hundred years old
and their movements all decline.
Is it because the times are different,
or have people lost the way?"
Qíbó replied,
"The people of high antiquity
who understood the Dao
patterned themselves on yin and yang,
harmonized themselves with the arts of calculation,
were moderate in eating and drinking,
had regular patterns of rising and resting,
and did not engage in reckless labor.
Therefore, they were able to keep their bodies and spirits together
and live out their natural lifespans,
People of the present age are not like that.
They take wine as drink,
and regard recklessness as normal.
They enter the bedroom while intoxicated,
exhausting their essence with desire,
dissipating their true nature,
not knowing how to maintain fullness,
and not regulating their spirit at the proper time.
They strive to gratify their hearts,
going against the joy of life.
Their daily life lacks moderation.
Therefore, they decline by the age of fifty.
上古时期，对通晓养生之道的圣人的教诲，
人们都能遵守。
对于四时不正之气，
能够及时回避，
思想上清静安闲，
无欲无求，真气深藏顺从，
精神持守于内而不耗散，
这样，疾病怎么会发生呢？
所以他们心志闲淑，私欲很少，
心情安宁，没有恐惧,
形体虽然劳动，但不过分疲倦。
真气从容和顺，
每个人的希望和要求，
都能满足。
无论吃什么都觉得甜美，
穿什么都觉得漂亮，
喜欢社会习俗，
and do not envy those above or below them.
Their people are therefore said to be simple.
Thus, cravings cannot tire their eyes,
and excessive desires cannot惑 (huò) mislead their hearts.
Whether foolish, wise, virtuous, or unworthy, they do not fear external things,
and therefore accord with the Dao.
The reason they can all live to be over a hundred years old,
and their movements do not decline,
is that their virtue is complete and without danger.
1.3 The Dì (帝) Emperor said:
"Are people who are old and have no children
exhausted in their talent and strength,
or is it simply the way of Heaven?"
Qíbó (歧伯) replied:
"A woman at seven years old,
her kidney Qi (腎氣) is flourishing,
her teeth change,
and her hair grows.
At fourteen, Tiānguǐ (天癸) arrives,
the Rèn (任) channel is open,
and the Tài chōng (太衝) channel is abundant.
Menstruation occurs regularly,
and therefore she can have children.
At twenty-one, her kidney Qi (腎氣) is balanced,
thus her wisdom teeth grow, Therefore, the real teeth grow and reach their peak length;
at four sevens (28 years old), the tendons and bones are firm,
the hair grows to its maximum length,
and the body is strong and vigorous.
At five sevens (35 years old),
the Yángmíng (陽明) meridian begins to decline,
the face begins to show signs of aging,
and the hair begins to fall out.
At six sevens (42 years old), the three Yáng (陽) meridians decline in the upper part of the body,
the face is completely withered,
and the hair begins to turn white.
At seven sevens (49 years old), the Rèn (任) meridian is deficient,
the Tài chōng (太衝) meridian declines,
the Tiān Guǐ (天癸) is exhausted,
the earth passage is not open,
therefore the form deteriorates and she is unable to have children.
男子八岁时，
肾气开始充实，
头发生长，
牙齿更换。
到了十六岁时，肾气盛满，
天癸发育成熟，
精气充满，如男女交合，
就能生育子女了。
到了二十四岁，肾气平和，
筋骨强劭，
智齿生长，身高也长到最高了。
到了三十二岁，筋骨粗壮，
肌肉充实。
到了四十岁，肾气开始衰退，
头发开始脱落，
teeth become withered.
At sixty-eight, the *yáng qì* declines and exhausts upwards,
the face becomes withered,
the hair at the temples turns gray.
At seventy-eight, the liver *qì* declines,
the sinews can no longer move,
*tiān guǐ* is exhausted,
essence is diminished,
the kidney storage declines,
the body is entirely exhausted.
At eighty-eight, the teeth and hair fall out.
The kidneys govern water,
receiving the essence of the five viscera and six bowels and storing it.
Therefore, when the five viscera are flourishing, they are able to discharge.
Now, the five viscera are all declining,
the sinews and bones are relaxed and weakened,
*tiān guǐ* is completely exhausted.
Therefore, the hair at the temples is white,
the body is heavy,
walking is unsteady,
and there are no children.
The Dì
Why is it that some are old but still have children?
Qí Bó
This is because their natural lifespan is excessively long,
their qi and vessels are constantly open,
and their kidney qi is abundant.
Even though they have children,
the men will not exceed the limit of eight eights (64 years old),
and the women will not exceed the limit of seven sevens (49 years old),
and the essence of heaven and earth will be exhausted.
The Yellow Emperor (Huángdì) said:
Those who possess the Dao (Dào)
are all over a hundred years old,
can they still have children?
Qíbó said:
Those who possess the Dao (Dào)
can reverse aging and preserve their form.
Even though their bodies are old,
they can still have children.
1.4 The Yellow Emperor (Huángdì) said:
I have heard that
in ancient times there were True Men (zhēnrén)
who grasped and lifted heaven and earth,
controlled yin and yang,
inhaled the essence of qi,
stood alone and guarded their spirit,
their muscles were unified as one,
therefore they could live as long as heaven and earth,
without end.
This is how they lived according to the Dao (Dào).
In the era of high antiquity,
there were perfected people (zhì rén)
who possessed pure virtue and complete Dao,
were in harmony with yin and yang,
regulated themselves to the four seasons,
departed from the world and separated from common customs,
accumulated essence and preserved their spirit,
wandered between heaven and earth,
and extended their vision and hearing beyond the eight directions.
These were those who increased their lifespan
and grew strong,
and also returned to be true people (zhēn rén).
Next were the sages (shèng rén),
who dwelt in the harmony of heaven and earth,
followed the principles of the eight winds,
adapted their desires to the ways of the world,
had no angry or hateful thoughts,
acted without wanting to depart from the world,
wore ceremonial robes,
conducted themselves without wanting to appear peculiar to customs,
did not outwardly exhaust their bodies with affairs,
and inwardly had no worries of thought.
They made tranquility and pleasure their task,
and self-satisfaction their accomplishment.
Their forms did not decay,
and their spirits did not scatter.
They could also live to be a hundred.
Next were the worthies (xián rén),
It models Heaven and Earth,
resembles the Sun and Moon,
distinguishes and arrays the stars and constellations,
complies with and follows Yin and Yang,
differentiates the four seasons,
aligning from ancient times,
harmonizing with the Dao,
and can also enable one to increase lifespan
and have an ultimate time.
The Second Discourse on the Great Treatise on Regulating the Spirit with the Four Qi.
2.1 In the three months of spring,
this is called expelling the old (陳 chén),
Heaven and Earth together generate,
the myriad things flourish,
retire late and rise early,
stroll broadly in the courtyard,
let the hair down and relax the body,
in order to allow the will (志 zhì) to be born,
give birth and do not kill,
give and do not take away,
reward and do not punish,
this is the response to the qi of spring,
the way to nurture life.
To go against it will injure the liver,
and in summer there will be transformations of cold,
and the support for growth will be diminished.
In the three months of summer,
This is called luxuriant flourishing;
it is when the Qi of Heaven and Earth intermingle,
and the myriad things blossom and bear fruit.
Sleep at night and rise early,
without being weary of the sun.
Let the will be without anger,
let the brilliance and vitality become luxuriant,
let the Qi be able to vent.
Be as if what you love is outside.
This is the correspondence to the Qi of summer,
the Dao of nourishing growth.
To go against it injures the heart;
in autumn, it becomes intermittent malaria;
what is received for storage is little;
in winter, it becomes a severe illness.
The three months of autumn,
are called equanimity.
The weather of Heaven becomes acute,
the Qi of Earth becomes clear.
Sleep early and rise early,
rise with the chickens.
Let the will be peaceful and tranquil,
in order to moderate the autumn punishments.
Gather and restrain the Shen Qi,
so that the autumn Qi is equable.
Do not let your will be outward-seeking,
so that the lung Qi is clear.
This is the correspondence to the Qi of autumn,
This concerns the Dao of nourishing and storing.
Reversing it injures the lungs.
In winter, it leads to diarrhea.
What is stored becomes little.
The three months of winter,
are called "closure and storage."
Water freezes, and the ground cracks.
Do not disturb the *yáng*.
Go to bed early and rise late,
waiting for the sunlight.
Make your will seem as if hiding or concealing,
as if you have private intentions,
as if you have already obtained something.
Leave the cold and approach warmth.
Do not allow the skin
to leak *qì* and be quickly depleted.
This is the correspondence to the *qì* of winter,
the Dao of nourishing storage.
Reversing it injures the kidneys.
In spring, it causes flaccidity and fainting.
What is fostered for growth becomes little.
2.2 The *tiān qì* (heavenly *qì*) is pure and bright.
Storing virtue without cease
therefore, it does not descend.
When the sky is darkened,
then the sun and moon are not bright.
Evil harms the empty orifices.
When the *yáng qì* is closed off,
and the *dì qì* bursts forth with brightness,
if the clouds and mists are not pure,
then the white dew will not descend in response from above.
If communication is not evident,
the mandate of the myriad things is not bestowed,
if it is not bestowed, then many famous trees will die.
If foul *qì* does not dissipate,
wind and rain are not regulated,
and white dew does not fall,
then the lush grasses and grains will not flourish.
If thieving winds frequently arrive,
and torrential rains frequently arise,
if Heaven and Earth and the four seasons do not protect each other,
and they lose harmony with the Dào,
then the thriving will be cut off and extinguished.
Only the sage follows it,
therefore their body has no strange illnesses,
the myriad things are not lost,
and vital *qì* is not exhausted.
If one goes against the *chūn qì* (spring *qì*),
then *shǎo yáng* (lesser *yáng*) will not be born,
and the *gān qì* (liver *qì*) will internally change.
If one goes against the *xià qì* (summer *qì*),
then *tài yáng* (greater *yáng*) will not grow,
and the *xīn qì* (heart *qì*) will internally become hollow.
If one goes against the *qiū qì* (autumn *qì*),
then *tài yīn* (greater *yīn*) will not gather,
The Lungs' *qì* is scorched and replete.
To go against the *qì* of winter,
then the *Shào Yīn* will not store,
and the Kidneys' *qì* will sink in isolation.
Now, the *yīn* and *yáng* of the four seasons,
are the root of all things.
Therefore, the sage nourishes *yáng* in spring and summer,
and nourishes *yīn* in autumn and winter,
in order to follow their root.
Thus, he rises and falls with all things at the gate of growth.
To go against their root
is to cut down their stem,
and destroy their essence.
2.3 Thus, *yīn* and *yáng* and the four seasons,
are the beginning and end of all things,
the root of life and death.
To go against them will cause disasters to arise;
to follow them will prevent severe illnesses from arising.
This is called attaining the Dao. The Dao
is what the sage practices,
and the fool carries.
Following *yīn* and *yáng* leads to life;
going against them leads to death.
Following them leads to order;
going against them leads to chaos.
Reversing compliance is called opposition;
this is called internal obstruction.
Therefore, the sage does not treat illness that has already manifested,
but treats illness before it manifests.
He does not govern disorder that has already arisen,
but governs disorder before it arises.
This is what is meant by that.
Indeed, to administer medicine after the illness has already developed,
to govern after the disorder has already arisen,
is like digging a well when already thirsty,
or forging an awl when already in a fight.
Is this not too late?
Chapter Three: On the Theory of Qi Connecting with Heaven
3.1 Huángdì said:
Now, from ancient times, those who connect with Heaven are the root of life,
rooted in the yin and yang between Heaven and Earth,
within the six directions.
Their qi connects to the weather through the nine regions, the nine orifices, the five viscera, and the twelve joints.
All connect with heavenly qi.
Its generation is five,
its qi is three.
Those who frequently violate this,
then pathogenic qi will harm people.
This is the root of life.
If the qi of blue Heaven is pure and clear,
then the will and intention are governed.
Following it, the yang qi is firm,
and even if there are rebellious evils,
they cannot harm it.
This is due to the sequence of the seasons.
Therefore, the sages transmit the spirit,
submit to the qi of the heavens,
and communicate with the spirits.
Losing this results in the internal closure of the nine orifices,
the external obstruction of the muscles,
and the defensive qi dispersing and disintegrating.
This is called self-harm,
a depletion of qi.
3.2.1 Yang qi is like the heavens and the sun;
if it loses its proper place,
then one's lifespan is shortened and one's virtue is not manifest.
Therefore, the movement of the heavens ought to be illuminated by the sun.
Thus, yang qi ascends upwards,
defending the exterior.
If affected by cold,
one desires to move like a hinge;
one's rising and resting is like being startled;
the spirit qi then floats.
If affected by heat,
with sweating and vexation, one then pants and gasps;
in stillness, one talks excessively;
the body is like burning charcoal;
the sweat comes out and scatters.
If affected by dampness,
the head is as if wrapped;
if damp heat is not expelled,
When the large sinews are contracted and shortened,
and the small sinews are relaxed and lengthened,
contraction and shortening cause stiffness,
relaxation and lengthening cause flaccidity.
When it arises from *qì*,
it causes swelling.
When the four limbs mutually substitute for each other,
the *yáng qì* is then exhausted.
3.2.2 *Yáng qì*:
when troubled by exertion, it expands;
when essence is exhausted, it accumulates;
in summer, it causes people to suffer from heat syncope (*jiānjué*).
The eyes become blind and cannot see,
the ears become blocked and cannot hear.
It collapses and crumbles like a ruined city,
gushing forth and unstoppable.
*Yáng qì*:
when greatly angered, the form and *qì* are severed,
and the blood accumulates upwards,
causing people to suffer from *bòjué*.
If the sinews are injured and relaxed,
it feels as if they cannot be contained;
sweat emerges with partial aversion to cold (*piān jù*),
causing people to suffer from hemiplegia (*piān kū*).
Sweating and exposure to dampness
then generate acne and sweat rash (*cuó fèi*).
Changes due to rich food (*gāoliáng*):
If large boils grow on the feet,
receive them as if holding emptiness.
Laboring and sweating exposed to the wind,
cold encroaching causes chapped skin (皻 chá).
Stagnation then becomes acne (痤 cuó).
3.2.3 Yang qi,
when refined, nourishes the spirit,
when gentle, nourishes the sinews.
If opening and closing is impeded,
cold qi follows,
and then large kyphosis (僂 lǚ) is produced.
When it penetrates the vessels, it becomes a fistula (瘻 lòu),
lingering in the flesh and skin.
If the qi of the acupoints is transformed thinly,
it transmits into excessive fear (善畏 shàn wèi),
and then into fright.
If yíng qi does not follow,
and rebels against the muscle texture,
then carbuncles and swellings are produced.
If the pò sweat is not completely exhausted,
the form is weak and the qi is depleted,
the acupoints and openings are closed,
and it develops into wind malaria (風瘧 fēng nüè).
Therefore, wind
is the beginning of all diseases.
If one is pure and still, then the flesh and skin close and resist,
even if there is a great wind with harsh poison,
Cannot harm it;
This is due to the order of the times.
Therefore, if an illness lasts long, it will transform and spread.
The upper and lower parts are not combined,
A good doctor will not treat it.
Therefore, if *yáng* accumulates, the disease leads to death,
And the *yáng qì* should be separated;
What is separated should be drained.
If not quickly and correctly treated,
A crude approach will ruin it.
3.2.4 Therefore, *yáng qì*
Governs the outside for a day.
At dawn, human *qì* is born.
At midday, *yáng qì* flourishes.
At sunset, *yáng qì* is already depleted,
And the *qì* gates then close.
Therefore, at dusk, gather and resist;
Do not disturb the muscles and bones;
Do not expose oneself to mist and dew.
To act contrary to these three times,
The body will then be weakened and frail.
3.3.1 Qí Bó 歧伯 said:
*Yīn*
Stores essence and initiates urgency.
*Yáng*
Defends the outside and provides firmness.
When *yīn* does not overcome its *yáng*,
then the pulse flow is weak and rapid,
and this results in mania.
When *yáng* does not overcome its *yīn*,
then the qi of the five viscera contend,
and the nine orifices are not unblocked.
Therefore, the sage arranges *yīn* and *yáng*
so that the sinews and vessels are harmonious,
the bones and marrow are firm,
and *qì* and blood all follow [their proper course].
If it is like this,
then the internal and external are harmonized,
evil cannot harm,
the ears and eyes are clear and bright,
and the *qì* is established as before.
3.3.2 When wind and perverse *qì* invade,
essence is then lost,
and evil harms the liver.
Because of this, if one eats until full,
the sinews and vessels become transversely loosened,
and dysentery becomes hemorrhoids.
Because of this, if one drinks heavily,
then the *qì* rebels.
Because of this, if one exerts great force,
the kidney *qì* is then injured,
and the high bones are then damaged.
Generally, the essentials of *yīn* and *yáng* [are such that]
When the yang is dense, it is firm;
if the two are not in harmony,
it is like spring without autumn,
like winter without summer.
Therefore, harmonizing them
is called the standard of a sage.
Therefore, strong yang cannot be dense,
and the yin qi will then be exhausted.
When the yin is balanced and the yang is stored,
the spirit will then be governed.
When yin and yang are separated and severed,
the essence and qi will then be exhausted.
Because of exposure to wind,
then cold and heat are produced.
3.3.3 Therefore, if one is injured by wind in the spring,
the evil qi will linger,
and then cause diarrhea.
If one is injured by heat in the summer,
in the autumn it will become intermittent malaria.
If one is injured by dampness in the autumn,
the qi will rise upward causing coughing,
and develop into flaccidity and syncope.
If one is injured by cold in the winter,
in the spring there will definitely be warm diseases.
The qi of the four seasons
mutually injure the five viscera.
3.3.4 The origin of *yīn*
lies fundamentally in the five flavors.
The five palaces of *yīn*
are injured by the five flavors.
Therefore, if the flavor is excessively sour,
the *qì* of the Liver is drawn upon,
and the *qì* of the Spleen is then exhausted.
If the flavor is excessively salty,
the *qì* of the large bones is strained,
the muscles shorten,
and the *qì* of the Heart is repressed.
If the flavor is excessively sweet,
the *qì* of the Heart is panting and full,
the complexion darkens, and the *qì* of the Kidneys is unbalanced.
If the flavor is excessively bitter,
the *qì* of the Spleen is not moistened,
and the *qì* of the Stomach becomes thick.
If the flavor is excessively pungent,
the sinews and vessels become flaccid and relaxed,
and the spirit is then impaired.
Therefore, carefully harmonize the five flavors,
and the bones will be upright and the sinews supple,
*qì* and blood will flow freely,
and the pores and skin will be dense.
If it is like this,
then the *qì* of the bones will be refined.
Carefully following the Dao according to the law,
one will long possess the mandate of heaven.
Chapter 4: Jīnkùi Zhēnyán Lùn (Golden Cabinet True Words Treatise)
4.1 The Yellow Emperor asked:
"Heaven has eight winds,
the body has five winds.
What are they?"
Qíbó replied:
"The eight winds give rise to evil influences,
which become the body's winds.
They attack the five viscera,
and these evil influences cause disease.
That which is called the victory of the four seasons
is that spring overcomes late summer,
late summer overcomes winter,
winter overcomes summer,
summer overcomes autumn,
and autumn overcomes spring.
This is what is meant by the victory of the four seasons.
The east wind is born in spring,
and disease manifests at the Liver Shu point,
and in the neck;
the south wind is born in summer,
and disease manifests at the Heart Shu point,
and in the chest and ribs;
the west wind is born in autumn,
and disease manifests at the Lung Shu point,
and in the shoulders and back;
the north wind is born in winter,
If the disease is located at Shènshū (腎俞),
it is in the loins and thighs;
the center corresponds to earth,
so if the disease is located at Píshū (脾俞),
it is in the spine.
Therefore, spring's qi causes diseases in the head,
summer's qi causes diseases in the viscera,
autumn's qi causes diseases in the shoulders and back,
winter's qi causes diseases in the four limbs.
Therefore, in spring, one is prone to nasal congestion and nosebleeds,
in mid-summer, one is prone to diseases of the chest and hypochondria,
in late summer, one is prone to profuse diarrhea and cold in the middle jiao,
in autumn, one is prone to wind-malaria,
in winter, one is prone to numbness and fainting.
Therefore, if one does not massage the qiāo (蹻) in winter,
one will not have nasal congestion and nosebleeds in spring.
If one does not get sick with neck problems in spring,
if one does not get sick with chest and hypochondriac issues in mid-summer,
if one does not get sick with profuse diarrhea and cold in the middle jiao in late summer,
if one does not get sick with wind-malaria in autumn,
if one does not get sick with numbness and fainting and food-induced diarrhea in winter,
and also sweats.
Now, essence (jīng 精) is the root of the body,
therefore, if one stores essence well, one will not suffer from febrile diseases in spring.
If one cannot sweat in the summer heat,
one will develop wind-malaria in the autumn.
This is the pulse method for a normal person.
4.2 Thus it is said:
within yin there is yin,
within yang there is yang.
From dawn to midday,
it is the yang of Heaven,
the yang within yang;
from midday to dusk,
it is the yang of Heaven,
the yin within yang;
from nightfall to the crowing of the rooster,
it is the yin of Heaven,
the yin within yin;
from the crowing of the rooster to dawn,
it is the yin of Heaven,
the yang within yin.
Therefore, humans also correspond to this.
Speaking of the yin and yang of humans,
the exterior is yang,
the interior is yin.
Speaking of the yin and yang of the human body,
the back is yang,
the abdomen is yin.
Speaking of the yin and yang of the Zàng (藏) and Fǔ (府) organs of the human body,
the Zàng organs are yin,
the Fǔ organs are yang.
The liver (Gān), heart (Xīn), spleen (Pí), lungs (Fèi), and kidneys (Shèn), the five Zàng organs,
are all yin.
The gallbladder (Dǎn), stomach (Wèi), large intestine (Dàcháng), small intestine (Xiǎocháng), bladder (Pángguāng), and Sanjiao (Sānjiāo), the six Fǔ organs,
All belong to Yang.
Therefore, what is meant by wanting to know the Yin within Yin,
and the Yang within Yang?
It is because winter diseases reside in Yin,
summer diseases reside in Yang,
spring diseases reside in Yin,
autumn diseases reside in Yang.
All are observed according to their location,
in order to apply acupuncture.
Therefore, the back is Yang,
and the Yang within Yang
is the heart (xīn);
the back is Yang,
and the Yin within Yang
is the lung (fèi);
the abdomen is Yin,
and the Yin within Yin
is the kidney (shèn);
the abdomen is Yin,
and the Yang within Yin
is the liver (gān);
the abdomen is Yin,
and the utmost Yin within Yin
is the spleen (pí).
These are all interrelated correspondences of Yin and Yang, exterior and interior, female and male.
Therefore, they correspond with the Yin and Yang of Heaven.
4.3 The Emperor (Dì) said:
Do the five viscera correspond to the four seasons?
Does each have its own receiving and accepting?
Qíbó said:
Yes. The east corresponds to the color green,
entering and connecting to the liver,
opening its orifice to the eyes,
storing essence in the liver.
Its disease manifests as fright and terror.
Its taste is sour,
its category is herbs and trees,
its animal is the chicken,
its grain is wheat,
it corresponds to the four seasons,
above it is the Jupiter (岁星 Suìxīng).
Therefore, the spring *qì* is located in the head.
Its musical note is *jué*,
its number is eight.
Therefore, one knows the disease is located in the sinews.
Its odor is rancid.
The south corresponds to the color red,
entering and connecting to the heart,
opening its orifice to the ears,
storing essence in the heart.
Therefore, the disease is located in the five viscera.
Its taste is bitter,
its category is fire,
its animal is the goat,
its grain is millet,
It corresponds to the four seasons;
above, it is the Flamboyant Star (Yínghuòxīng, Mars).
Therefore, one knows the disease is in the pulse.
Its note is zhǐ (徵).
Its number is seven.
Its odor is scorched.
The center is yellow.
It enters and communicates with the spleen.
It opens its orifice in the mouth.
It stores essence in the spleen.
Therefore, the disease is at the root of the tongue.
Its taste is sweet.
Its category is earth.
Its domestic animal is the ox.
Its grain is millet.
It corresponds to the four seasons;
above, it is the Saturn Star (Zhènxīng).
Therefore, one knows the disease is in the flesh.
Its note is gōng (宮).
Its number is five.
Its odor is fragrant.
The west is white.
It enters and communicates with the lungs.
It opens its orifice in the nose.
It stores essence in the lungs.
Therefore, the disease is in the back.
Its taste is pungent.
Its category is metal.
Its livestock is the horse (mǎ),
its grain is rice (dào),
it corresponds to the four seasons,
above it is the Tàibái star,
therefore one knows the disease is located in the skin and hair.
Its musical note is shāng,
its number is nine,
its odor is rancid.
The north is black,
it enters and connects to the kidney (shèn),
it opens its orifices in the two yīn,
it stores essence in the kidney (shèn),
therefore the disease is located in the crevices.
Its taste is salty,
its category is water,
its livestock is the pig (zhì),
its grain is beans (dòu),
it corresponds to the four seasons,
above it is the Chén star,
therefore one knows the disease is located in the bones.
Its musical note is yǔ,
its number is six,
its odor is rotten.
Therefore, one who is skilled in pulse diagnosis
carefully observes the five zàng and six fǔ organs,
observing one that goes against and one that follows,
the yīn and yáng, exterior and interior,
the principles of female and male,
Store it in your heart,
unite your mind with its essence.
Do not teach it to those who are unworthy,
do not impart its truth to those who are insincere.
This is called attaining the Dao.
Chapter 5: Yīnyáng Yìng Xiàng Dà Lùn (Great Treatise on the Correspondence of Yīn and Yáng)
5. 1 The Yellow Emperor (Huángdì) said:
Yīn and Yáng
are the Dao of Heaven and Earth,
the guiding principle of all things,
the parents of change,
the origin of life and death,
the dwelling place of spirit and clarity.
To treat illness, one must seek its root.
Therefore, the accumulation of Yáng becomes Heaven,
the accumulation of Yīn becomes Earth.
Yīn is stillness, Yáng is agitation;
Yáng generates, Yīn grows;
Yáng kills, Yīn stores.
Yáng transforms into Qì,
Yīn forms shape.
Extreme cold generates heat,
extreme heat generates cold.
Cold Qì generates turbidity,
hot Qì generates clarity.
If clear Qì is below,
it causes diarrhea with undigested food;
When turbid *qì* is above,
then bloating arises.
This is yin and yang acting in reverse,
a pattern of disease conforming and opposing.
5.2.1 Therefore, clear yang is heaven,
turbid yin is earth;
the earth's *qì* rises to become clouds,
the heaven's *qì* descends to become rain;
rain comes from the earth's *qì*,
clouds come from the heaven's *qì*.
5.2.2 Therefore, clear yang exits from the upper orifices,
turbid yin exits from the lower orifices;
clear yang emanates from the *còulǐ* (skin texture),
turbid yin travels to the five *zàng* organs;
clear yang fills the four limbs,
turbid yin returns to the six *fǔ* organs.
5.2.3 Water is yin,
fire is yang,
yang is *qì*,
yin is flavor.
Flavor returns to form,
form returns to *qì*,
*qì* returns to essence (*jīng*),
essence (*jīng*) returns to transformation,
essence (*jīng*) nourishes *qì*,
Form eats flavor,
transformation generates essence,
qi generates form.
Flavor injures form,
qi injures essence,
essence transforms into qi,
qi is injured by flavor.
Yin flavors exit the lower orifices,
yang qi exits the upper orifices.
Thick flavors are yin,
thin is yang within yin.
Thick qi is yang,
thin is yin within yang.
Thick flavors cause purging,
thin causes passage.
Thin qi causes discharge,
thick causes fever.
The qi of strong fire declines,
the qi of weak fire flourishes.
Strong fire consumes qi,
qi consumes weak fire.
Strong fire scatters qi,
weak fire generates qi.
Qi and flavor,
acrid and sweet, dispersing, are yang,
sour and bitter, surging and draining, are yin.
5.2.4 When yin prevails, yang becomes ill,
When Yáng exceeds, then Yīn falls ill.
When Yáng exceeds, there is heat.
When Yīn exceeds, there is cold.
Extreme cold generates heat.
Extreme heat generates cold.
Cold injures the form (xíng).
Heat injures the Qi (qì).
Qi injury causes pain.
Form injury causes swelling.
Therefore, if pain precedes swelling,
it is Qi injuring form.
If swelling precedes pain,
it is form injuring Qi.
When wind prevails, there is movement.
When heat prevails, there is swelling.
When dryness prevails, there is desiccation.
When cold prevails, there is edema.
When dampness prevails, there is maceration.
5.2.5 Heaven has four seasons and five elements,
for generating, growing, harvesting, and storing,
and for generating cold, heat, dryness, dampness, and wind.
Man has five viscera,
which transform the five Qi,
to generate joy, anger, sorrow, grief, and fear.
Therefore, joy and anger injure Qi,
cold and heat injure form.
Sudden anger injures Yīn.
Excessive joy injures the *yáng*.
The *jué* (counterflow) *qì* rises upwards,
Filling the vessels and departing from the form (body).
Joy and anger without moderation,
Cold and heat in excess,
Life will not be secure.
Therefore, extreme *yīn* inevitably transforms into *yáng*,
And extreme *yáng* inevitably transforms into *yīn*.
Therefore, it is said:
If one is injured by cold in winter,
One will inevitably suffer from febrile disease in spring;
If one is injured by wind in spring,
One will develop *sūn xiè* (dysentery) in summer;
If one is injured by heat in summer,
One will inevitably suffer from *jiē nüè* (a type of malaria) in autumn;
If one is injured by dampness in autumn,
One will then develop coughs.
5.3 The Dì (Emperor) said:
I have heard that the ancient sages,
Discussed the structure of the human body,
Distinguished and classified the Zàng (organs) and Fǔ (bowels),
Precisely connected the channels and vessels,
Interconnected the six directions (universe),
Each following its own channel,
The *qì* points' locations each have their names,
The ravines and valleys belonging to the bones all have their origins,
Dividing the regions, flowing in opposite directions,
Each has its own order and principle;
the four seasons and *yīn* and *yáng*;
all are fully managed and regulated;
the correspondence of exterior and interior;
all have surface and substance.
Is this truly so?
Qíbó 岐伯 replied:
The east generates wind;
wind generates wood;
wood generates sourness;
sourness generates the liver;
the liver generates sinews;
sinews generate the heart;
the liver governs the eyes.
In the heavens, it is *xuán* 玄;
in humans, it is the Dào 道;
on earth, it is transformation.
Transformation generates the five flavors;
the Dào 道 generates wisdom;
*xuán* 玄 generates spirit.
Spirit in the heavens is wind;
on earth is wood;
in the body is sinew;
in the viscera is the liver;
in color is green/blue;
in sound is *jué* 角;
in voice is shouting;
in movement is grasping;
In the orifice, it is the eyes;
In taste, it is sour;
In emotion, it is anger.
Anger injures the liver;
Grief overcomes anger;
Wind injures the sinews;
Dryness overcomes wind;
Sourness injures the sinews;
Pungency overcomes sourness.
The South generates heat;
Heat generates fire;
Fire generates bitterness;
Bitterness generates the heart;
The heart generates blood;
Blood generates the spleen;
The heart governs the tongue.
In the heavens, it is heat;
On earth, it is fire;
In the body, it is the vessels;
In the organs, it is the heart;
In color, it is red;
In sound, it is the zhǐ (徵) note;
In voice, it is laughter;
In change, it is worry;
In the orifice, it is the tongue;
In taste, it is bitter;
In emotion, it is joy.
Joy injures the heart;
*Kǒng* overcomes *xǐ*;
Heat injures *qì*;
Cold overcomes heat;
Bitter injures *qì*;
Salty overcomes bitter.
The center generates dampness;
Dampness generates earth;
Earth generates sweetness;
Sweetness generates the spleen;
The spleen generates flesh;
Flesh generates the lungs;
The spleen governs the mouth.
In the heavens, it is dampness;
On earth, it is earth;
In the body, it is flesh;
In the organs, it is the spleen;
In color, it is yellow;
In sound, it is *gōng* (the first note in the pentatonic scale);
In voice, it is singing;
In movement, it is hiccupping;
In the orifices, it is the mouth;
In taste, it is sweet;
In emotion, it is pensiveness.
Pensiveness injures the spleen;
Anger overcomes pensiveness;
Dampness injures flesh;
Wind overcomes dampness;
Sweetness injures flesh;
Sourness overcomes sweetness.
The west generates dryness,
dryness generates metal,
metal generates pungency,
pungency generates the lungs,
the lungs generate skin and hair,
skin and hair generate the kidneys,
The lungs govern the nose.
In the heavens, it is dryness,
on earth, it is metal,
in the body, it is skin and hair,
in the organs, it is the lungs,
in color, it is white,
in music, it is the *shāng* note,
in sound, it is weeping,
in movement, it is coughing,
in the orifices, it is the nose,
in taste, it is pungent,
in the emotions, it is worry.
Worry damages the lungs,
joy overcomes worry;
heat damages the skin and hair,
cold overcomes heat;
pungency damages the skin and hair,
bitterness overcomes pungency.
The north generates cold,
cold generates water,
water generates saltiness,
Salty flavor engenders the Kidneys;
the Kidneys engender bone marrow;
the bone marrow engenders the Liver;
the Kidneys govern the ears.
In the heavens, it is cold;
on earth, it is water;
in the body, it is bones;
in the viscera, it is the Kidneys;
in color, it is black;
in sound, it is the yǔ (羽) note;
in vocalization, it is groaning;
in change and movement, it is trembling;
in the orifices, it is the ears;
in taste, it is salty;
in the will, it is fear.
Fear injures the Kidneys;
contemplation overcomes fear;
cold injures the blood;
dryness overcomes cold;
saltiness injures the blood;
sweetness overcomes saltiness.
Therefore, it is said:
Heaven and earth
are the upper and lower (limits) of all things;
Yīn and Yáng
are to blood and qì what male and female are;
left and right
are the pathways of Yīn and Yáng;
Water and fire are
the signs of *yīn* and *yáng*.
*Yīn* and *yáng* are
the origin of all things.
Therefore, it is said:
*Yīn* is within,
guarding *yáng*;
*yáng* is without,
employing *yīn*.
5.4.1 The Yellow Emperor (Dì) said:
How do we follow *yīn* and *yáng*?
Qíbó said:
When *yáng* prevails, the body becomes hot,
the pores close,
breathing becomes coarse, causing one to bend over and look up.
No sweat is produced, and there is heat,
the teeth are dry, with vexation, distress, and abdominal distention,
leading to death; able to withstand winter but not summer.
When *yīn* prevails, the body becomes cold, and sweat is produced,
the body is constantly cool,
with frequent shivering and coldness,
coldness leads to *jué* (reversal/counterflow),
*jué* leads to abdominal distention,
leading to death; able to withstand summer but not winter.
These are the changes of *yīn* and *yáng* overcoming each other,
the forms and abilities of disease.
5.4.2 The Emperor asked:
"How can these two be regulated?"
What should I do?
Qíbó said:
"If one can understand the 'seven diminutions and eight augmentations',
then these two can be regulated.
If one does not know how to apply this,
then it is a sign of premature decline.
At the age of forty,
the *yīn qì* naturally halves,
and one's daily activities decline.
At the age of fifty,
the body becomes heavy,
and the ears and eyes are no longer sharp.
At the age of sixty,
the *yīn* withers,
the *qì* greatly declines,
the nine orifices become impaired,
the lower body is deficient while the upper body is full,
and tears and mucus flow together.
Therefore, it is said:
'Knowing it, one becomes strong;
not knowing it, one becomes old.'
Thus, they emerge from the same source but are named differently.
The wise observe similarities,
the foolish observe differences.
The foolish are deficient,
the wise have abundance.
If there is surplus, then the ears and eyes are sharp and clear,
the body is light and strong,
the old are rejuvenated,
the strong are even more strengthened.
Therefore, the sage engages in effortless actions (wúwéi zhī shì),
enjoys the ability of serenity and tranquility (tián dàn),
and freely indulges the will in upholding emptiness and nothingness (xū wú zhī shǒu).
Therefore, life has no end,
and ends together with Heaven and Earth.
This is how the sage governs the body.
5.4.3 Heaven is insufficient in the northwest,
therefore the northwest is Yin,
and a person's right ears and eyes are not as bright as the left.
Earth is incomplete in the southeast,
therefore the southeast is Yang,
and a person's left hands and feet are not as strong as the right.
The Emperor (Dì) said:
Why is this so?
Qí Bó said:
The east is Yang,
for those who are Yang, their essence is gathered above (bìng yú shàng).
Gathered above (bìng yú shàng),
then the upper part is bright and the lower part is empty,
therefore the ears and eyes are sharp and clear,
but the hands and feet are not convenient.
The west is Yin,
for those who are Yin, their essence is gathered below (bìng yú xià).
If (the evil influences) gather below,
then the lower part becomes replete while the upper part becomes deficient.
Therefore, the ears and eyes are not sharp,
but the hands and feet are agile.
Therefore, when both are affected by evil influences,
if it is in the upper part, the right side is more severe,
and if it is in the lower part, the left side is more severe.
This is what Tiāndì (Heaven and Earth), Yīnyáng (Yin and Yang) cannot completely encompass,
so evil resides in it.
Therefore, Heaven has essence,
Earth has form,
Heaven has eight cardinal points,
Earth has five *lǐ* (里, traditional unit of distance),
therefore, they can be the parents of all things.
Pure *yáng* ascends to Heaven,
turbid *yīn* returns to Earth.
Therefore, the movement and stillness of Heaven and Earth,
the spirits and brilliance are the governing principles.
Therefore, it can produce growth, gathering,
ending and beginning again.
Only the wise person matches Heaven above to nourish the head,
and imitates Earth below to nourish the feet,
and in the middle, relies on human affairs to nourish the five viscera.
The Qi of Heaven communicates with the lungs,
the Qi of Earth communicates with the throat,
the Qi of wind communicates with the liver,
the Qi of thunder communicates with the heart,
the Qi of grains communicates with the spleen,
The qi of rain corresponds to the kidneys.
The six meridians are like rivers,
the intestines and stomach are like the sea,
and the nine orifices are like the qi where water flows into.
Taking Heaven and Earth as its Yin and Yang,
the Yang's perspiration
is named after Heaven and Earth's rain;
the Yang's qi
is named after Heaven and Earth's violent wind.
Violent qi resembles thunder,
rebellious qi resembles the sun.
Therefore, if treatment does not follow the laws of Heaven
and does not utilize the principles of Earth,
then disasters will arrive.
5.4.4 Therefore, when evil wind arrives,
it is as swift as wind and rain.
Therefore, a good healer treats the skin and hair,
next treats the muscles and skin,
next treats the tendons and vessels,
next treats the six fu organs,
and finally treats the five zang organs.
To treat the five zang organs
is to be half dead and half alive.
Therefore, the evil qi of Heaven,
when contacted, harms the five zang organs;
the cold and heat of water and grain,
when contacted, harms the six fu organs;
The dampness of the earth,
when perceived, harms the skin, flesh, sinews, and vessels.
Therefore, those skilled in using needles
draw Yang from Yin,
draw Yin from Yang,
treat the left from the right,
treat the right from the left,
know the other through myself,
know the interior through the exterior,
observe the principles of excess and deficiency,
perceive the slight to detect the fault,
and use it without danger.
Those skilled in diagnosis
observe the complexion and palpate the pulse,
first distinguishing Yin and Yang;
examine the clear and turbid,
and know the affected areas;
observe the breathing,
listen to the sounds,
and know the source of suffering;
observe the balance of weights and measures,
and know the primary cause of the illness.
Palpate the cùn chǐ,
observe the floating, sinking, slippery, and rough (qualities),
and know the origin of the illness;
treat with no excess,
and diagnose without error.
Therefore, it is said:
When illness first begins,
it can be treated by acupuncture;
when it is at its peak,
one can only wait for it to decline.
Therefore, when it is mild, encourage it to spread outward;
when it is severe, diminish it;
when it is waning, make it manifest.
If the form (xíng) is deficient,
warm it with *qì*;
if the *jīng* is insufficient,
replenish it with flavors (taste).
If it (the illness) is located high (in the body),
then cause it to move upward and out;
if it is located low (in the body),
draw it downward and exhaust it;
if there is fullness in the middle (of the body),
drain it from within;
if there is evil (xié) present,
soak the form to induce sweating;
if it is located in the skin,
sweat it out and release it;
if it is violent and strong,
press down and restrain it;
if it is substantial,
scatter it and drain it.
Examine its *yīn* and *yáng* aspects
in order to distinguish between softness and strength;
treat *yáng* diseases by treating *yīn*;
Yīn (陰) diseases are treated by addressing yáng (陽),
stabilize their xuè qì (血氣),
each guarding its territory.
If the blood is replete, it should be drained;
if the qì (氣) is deficient, it should be guided and drawn forth.
Chapter Six: Discussion on the Separation and Union of Yīn and Yáng
6.1 The Yellow Emperor (Huángdì, 黃帝) asked:
"I have heard that Heaven is yáng (陽),
and Earth is yīn (陰);
the Sun is yáng (陽),
and the Moon is yīn (陰);
large and small months total three hundred and sixty days to form one year,
and man should also correspond to this.
Now, the three yīn (陰) and three yáng (陽)
do not correspond to yīn (陰) and yáng (陽).
What is the reason for this?"
Qíbó (歧伯) replied:
"Yīn (陰) and yáng (陽)
can be counted to ten,
extended to a hundred,
counted to a thousand,
extended to ten thousand.
The greatness of ten thousand is beyond reckoning,
yet its essence is one.
Heaven covers and Earth supports,
and myriad things come into being.
Those that have not yet emerged from the earth
What is called the Hidden Abode
, is named the Yin within Yin.
That which emerges from the earth
, is called the Yang within Yin.
Yang provides the correctness,
Yin takes charge.
Therefore, growth is due to spring,
development is due to summer,
harvest is due to autumn,
storage is due to winter.
Losing the norm, then Heaven and Earth are blocked in all directions.
The transformations of Yin and Yang,
as they are in humans,
are also enumerable.
6.2 The Dì [帝] said:
I wish to hear about the separation and union of the Three Yin and Three Yang.
Qíbó [歧伯] said:
The Sage stands facing south,
the front is called Guǎngmíng [廣明],
the back is called Tàichōng [太衝].
The region of Tàichōng [太衝],
is named Shǎoyīn [少陰].
Above Shǎoyīn [少陰],
is named Tàiyáng [太陽].
Tàiyáng's [太陽] root arises from the utmost Yin,
and connects to the Gate of Life (Mìngmén [命門]),
it is named the Yang within Yin.
That which rises from the middle of the body,
is called Guǎngmíng.
Below Guǎngmíng,
it is called Tàiyīn.
Before Tàiyīn,
it is called Yángmíng.
The Yángmíng originates at Lìduì,
and is called the yang within yin.
The exterior of Juéyīn,
is called Shǎoyáng.
The Shǎoyáng originates at Qiàoyīn,
and is called the lesser yang within yin.
Therefore, the separation and union of the three yang [channels]:
the Tàiyáng is the opening,
the Yángmíng is the closing,
the Shǎoyáng is the hinge.
These three channels
must not lose connection with each other,
they should be substantial and not superficial,
and are called one yang.
6.3 The Emperor said:
I would like to hear about the three yin [channels].
Qíbó said:
That which is external is yang,
that which is internal is yin,
therefore the middle is yin.
Its flow is downward,
It is named Tài Yīn.
The root of Tài Yīn originates at Yǐnbái,
named the Yin within Yin.
After Tài Yīn,
it is named Shǎo Yīn.
The root of Shǎo Yīn originates at Yǒngquán,
named the Lesser Yin within Yin.
Before Shǎo Yīn,
it is named Jué Yīn.
The root of Jué Yīn originates at Dàdūn,
the absolute Yin of Yin,
named the absolute Yin within Yin.
Therefore, in the separation and combination of the three Yins,
Tài Yīn is the opening (Kāi),
Jué Yīn is the closing (Hé),
Shǎo Yīn is the pivot (Shū).
These three meridians
must not lose their relationship to each other.
Gathering without sinking,
is called One Yin.
Yin and Yang intermingling,
accumulate and transmit to form a cycle,
Qi inside and form outside, thus completing each other.
Chapter Seven: A Separate Discussion on Yin and Yang
7.1 The Yellow Emperor asked:
"Humans have four meridians and twelve collaterals,
what does this mean?"
Qí Bó answered,
"The four conduits correspond to the four seasons,
the twelve collaterals correspond to the twelve months,
and the twelve months correspond to the twelve pulses.
Pulses have Yin and Yang.
Knowing Yang means knowing Yin,
and knowing Yin means knowing Yang.
Generally, there are five Yangs,
five times five is twenty-five Yangs.
What is called Yin
is the true zàng organs;
if they manifest, it indicates failure,
and failure inevitably leads to death.
What is called Yang
is the Yang of the stomach cavity.
Differentiating Yang allows [one to] know the location of the disease;
differentiating Yin allows [one to] know the time of life and death.
The three Yangs are in the head,
the three Yins are in the hand—
this is what is called the 'one.'
Differentiating Yang allows [one to] know the times to avoid with disease;
differentiating Yin allows [one to] know the time of life and death.
Carefully familiarize yourself with Yin and Yang,
and do not consult with others about it.
What is meant by Yin and Yang:
That which goes is Yin,
that which arrives is Yang;
stillness is Yin,
movement is Yang;
slowness is Yin,
rapidity is Yang.
Generally, those who hold a true pulse, where the deep pulse is hidden,
if the liver pulse reaches a suspended and cut-off state quickly,
death will occur in eighteen days;
if the heart pulse reaches a suspended and cut-off state,
death will occur in nine days;
if the lung pulse reaches a suspended and cut-off state,
death will occur in twelve days;
if the kidney pulse reaches a suspended and cut-off state,
death will occur in seven days;
if the spleen pulse reaches a suspended and cut-off state,
death will occur in four days.
7.2 It says:
A disease of the Two Yang
originates in the heart and spleen,
and involves inability to hide and crouch,
and cessation of menstruation in women;
if it transforms into *fēng xiāo* (wind wasting),
or if it transforms into *xī bēn* (rushing respiration),
death will occur and it cannot be treated.
It says: A disease of the Three Yang
To manifest as chills and fever;
Below, to become carbuncles and swellings;
And to become flaccid paralysis, or cramps in the calf;
What it transmits to is *Suǒzé*;
What it transmits to is *Tuíshàn*.
It is said: If *Yī Yáng* manifests illness,
There will be shortness of breath, frequent coughing, and frequent diarrhea;
What it transmits to is heart pain;
What it transmits to is obstruction.
If *Èr Yáng Yī Yīn* manifests illness,
It governs fright and back pain,
Frequent belching and frequent yawning,
Named *Fēngjué* (Wind Reversal).
If *Èr Yīn Yī Yáng* manifests illness,
There will be frequent bloating, fullness in the chest, and frequent gasping.
If *Sān Yáng Sān Yīn* manifests illness,
It becomes one-sided paralysis and flaccid debility,
The four limbs cannot be lifted.
7.3 Drumming the one *Yáng* is called a hook (*gōu*);
Drumming the one *Yīn* is called hair (*máo*);
Drumming when *Yáng* is excessively rapid is called string (*xián*);
Drumming when *Yáng* arrives and then stops is called stone (*shí*);
When *Yīn* and *Yáng* pass each other it is called trickling (*liū*).
When *Yīn* struggles within,
And *Yáng* is disturbed outside,
And the corporeal soul's sweat is not stored,
The four reversals arise,
When it rises, it fumes the lungs,
causing a person to wheeze.
Where *yin* is produced,
harmony at the root is called harmony.
Therefore, when *gang* meets *gang*,
*yang qi* scatters and breaks apart,
and *yin qi* then perishes.
If it is muddy, *gang* and *rou* are not harmonious,

Therefore, poisonous drugs
also come from the West.
12.3 The North is the region where Heaven and Earth conceal and store.
Its land is hilly and elevated.
It is windy, cold, and icy.
Its people delight in living in the wilderness and eating dairy.
Cold is stored within, causing fullness as a disease.
Their treatment is suitable for moxibustion.
Therefore, moxibustion
also comes from the North.
12.4 The South is the region where Heaven and Earth nurture and grow,
the place where *yáng* is most abundant.
Its land is low-lying.
Beneath that land,
the soil and water are weak,
a place where mists and dews gather.
The people there are fond of sour tastes and eat fermented foods.
Therefore, the people there are all fine-skinned and reddish in color.
Their diseases are contractures and numbness.
Their treatment is suited to fine needles.
Therefore, the nine needles
also came from the south.
12.5 Those of the center:
Their land is flat and damp.
Heaven and earth bring forth the myriad things there in abundance.
The people there eat a mixed diet and do not labor much.
Therefore, their diseases are mostly flaccidity, collapse, cold, and fever.
Their treatment is suited to guiding and stretching exercises and massage.
Therefore, guiding and stretching exercises and massage
also came from the center.
Therefore, the sage combines methods to treat,
each obtaining what is suitable for them.
Therefore, the reason why treatments differ but all diseases are cured
is that they grasp the essence of the disease
and understand the grand principles of treatment.
*Yí Jīng Biàn Qì Lùn Piān* (Treatise on Shifting Essence and Altering *Qì*) Thirteenth
13.1 The Yellow Emperor asked, saying:
"I have heard that the treatment of disease in ancient times
only involved shifting essence and altering *qì*,
It could be treated with Zhù Yóu alone.
In the current age, when treating illnesses,
poisonous medicines treat the interior,
acupuncture and stones treat the exterior,
sometimes curing and sometimes not,
why is this?
Qí Bó answered,
"In ancient times, people lived amongst birds and beasts,
moving around to avoid the cold,
dwelling in the shade to avoid the heat.
Inside, they had no burden of affections,
outside, they had no concern for officialdom.
This was a time of tranquility,
and evil could not deeply penetrate.
Therefore, poisonous medicines could not treat the interior,
acupuncture and stones could not treat the exterior,
thus, they could simply shift the spirit and use Zhù Yóu.
The current age is not like that;
worries and anxieties burden the interior,
hardship and toil injure the exterior,
moreover, they lose the following of the four seasons,
and go against what is proper for cold and heat.
Bandit winds frequently arrive,
and deficient evils come morning and night,
penetrating inward to the five viscera and bone marrow,
and injuring outward the orifices, skin, and flesh.
Therefore, small illnesses must become severe,
and large illnesses must result in death;
Therefore, Zhù Yóu (祝由) cannot be stopped.
13.2 The Emperor said:
"Excellent. I wish to personally attend to patients,
observe life and death,
resolve doubts and uncertainties,
and desire to know the essential principles,
as clear as the light of the sun and moon.
May I have the opportunity to hear them?"
Qí Bó (歧伯) said:
"Complexion and pulse are what
the Supreme Being values,
and what the former masters transmitted.
In ancient times, they employed Jiè Dài Jì (僦貸季),
to examine the complexion and pulse, thereby communicating with the spiritual realm.
Integrating them with the four seasons (metal, wood, water, fire, earth), the eight winds, and the six directions,
he did not deviate from their norm.
He changed and shifted accordingly
to observe their subtleties
to understand their essence.
If you wish to know the essence, then complexion and pulse are the key.
Complexion corresponds to the sun,
pulse corresponds to the moon.
Constantly seek their essence,
and that is the essence indeed.
The changes in complexion
correspond to the pulse of the four seasons.
This is what *Shàngdì* 上帝 values,
because it aligns with the spirits and intelligence;
therefore, it distances one from death and brings one closer to life.
The path to life is extended,
and it is called sage kingship.
In the middle ages, treating disease
involved arriving [early] and treating it.
Decoctions for ten days
were used to remove the diseases of the eight winds and five *bì* (numbness) afflictions.
If after ten days it did not stop,
treatment involved the branches of *cǎo sū* 草蘇 and *cǎo gāi* 草荄,
with the root and branch assisting each other.
Once the superficial and fundamental aspects were grasped,
the evil *qì* would then submit.
The way of treating disease in later ages is not like this.
Treatments are not rooted in the four seasons;
one does not understand the sun and moon,
nor does one examine the reverse and following order.
After the disease has already taken shape,
one then wants to use minute needles to treat the exterior,
and decoctions to treat the interior.
Crude craftsmen are reckless,
thinking it can be attacked.
Therefore, the disease does not end,
and new diseases arise again.
13.3 The *Dì* 帝 (Yellow Emperor) said,
"I wish to hear the essential path."
Qí Bó said:
The essential principle of treatment
is never to disregard complexion and pulse.
Applying it without hesitation
is the grand rule of treatment.
If one acts contrary to or compliant with the proper progression
and fails to grasp the superficial and fundamental aspects
it is like losing the spirit or losing the country.
Casting off the old and embracing the new
is the way to attain the state of a true person.
The Yellow Emperor said:
I have heard the essentials from you, Master.
Master said that treatment cannot depart from complexion and pulse;
this is what I understand.
Qí Bó said:
The ultimate of treatment lies in "oneness."
The Yellow Emperor said:
What is meant by "oneness"?
Qí Bó said:
"Oneness"
is attained by reliance.
The Yellow Emperor said:
How so?
Qí Bó said:
Close the doors and block the windows,
connect with the patient,
repeatedly inquire about their condition,
and follow their inclinations.
Dé shén zhě chāng,
shī shén zhě wáng.
Dì yuē:
Shàn.
Tāng Yè Láo Lǐ Lùn Piān Dì Shísì
14.1 Huángdì asked:
"How are wǔgǔ tāngyè (decoction of five grains) and láolǐ (cloudy sweet wine) made?"
Qíbó replied:
"One must use rice,
and cook it with rice straw.
Rice is whole,
rice straw is firm."
The Emperor said:
"Why is that so?"
Qíbó said:
"This is because they have obtained the harmony of heaven and earth,
and the suitability of high and low;
therefore, they can be completely whole.
Being felled and harvested at the right time,
therefore, it can be completely firm."
The Emperor said:
"The ancient sages made tāngyè and láolǐ,
but made them without using them,
why?"
Qíbó said:
"From ancient times, the sages made tāngyè and láolǐ
It was thought to be for preparedness.
In ancient times, decoctions were made,
and therefore made but not taken.
In the middle ages,
morality gradually declined,
and pathogenic factors arrived from time to time.
Taking them was completely safe.
The Emperor said:
Why is it that in the present age, they are not necessarily effective?
Qíbó 岐伯 said:
In the present age,
it is necessary to use potent drugs to attack the interior,
and *biǎn* stones, needles, and moxibustion to treat the exterior.
14.2 The Emperor said:
Why is it that the body is exhausted and the blood depleted, yet no results are achieved?
Qíbó 岐伯 said:
The *shén* is not employed.
The Emperor said:
What does it mean that the *shén* is not employed?
Qíbó 岐伯 said:
Needling and stone (therapy) are the *dào*.
If the *jīngshén* does not advance,
and the will and intent are not governed,
then the disease cannot be cured.
Now, if the *jīng* is damaged and the *shén* departs,
the *yíng* and *wèi* cannot be restored.
Why?
Desires and cravings are endless,
and worries and anxieties do not cease.
The essence and qi are relaxed and broken down,
*Róng* is deficient, *Wèi* is removed.
Therefore, the spirit departs from it, and the illness does not heal.
14.3 The Emperor said:
"When disease begins,
it is extremely subtle and extremely refined,
and it must first enter and collect in the skin.
Now, good doctors all say:
'When the disease is fully formed and called 'rebellious,'
then needles and stones cannot cure it,
and good medicine cannot reach it.'
Now, good doctors all obtain their methods,
guard their numbers,
relatives, brothers, those near and far, sounds are heard daily in their ears,
the five colors are seen daily in their eyes,
and yet the illness does not heal.
Is it not too late?"
Qíbó said:
"Disease is the root,
the doctor is the branch.
If the root and branch are not obtained,
the evil qi will not be subdued.
This is what is meant by this."
14.4 The Emperor said:
If there are those whose condition did not arise from the slightest ailment,
and the *yáng* of the five viscera is exhausted,
the fluids fill the body's exterior,
their *pò* spirit dwells alone,
the solitary essence is within,
and the *qì* is depleted externally,
the body cannot be kept warm by clothing,
this is when the four extremities are in urgent motion and the center is disturbed,
it means the *qì* is resisted internally,
while the body is dissipated externally,
how should it be treated?
Qí Bó said:
"Treat it with balanced and fair measures,
remove stagnant and decayed matter,
slightly move the four extremities,
keep them warmly clothed,
and apply oblique acupuncture to the affected areas,
in order to restore the body's form.
Open the ghost gate,
cleanse the pure mansion,
administer the essence at the proper time,
so that the five *yáng* will be distributed,
and cleanse the five viscera,
thus the essence will naturally regenerate,
the body will naturally thrive,
bone and flesh will mutually protect each other,
and the great *qì* will then be balanced."
The Emperor said:
Good.
Jade Tablet Discussion on Essentials, Chapter Fifteen
15.1 The Yellow Emperor, Huángdì, asked:
"I have heard that the methods of measuring, kuídù, and assessing extraordinary conditions, qíhéng,
have different applications.
How should they be used?"
Qíbó replied:
"Measuring, kuídù,
is for gauging the shallowness or depth of a disease.
Assessing extraordinary conditions, qíhéng,
refers to unusual illnesses.
Allow me to explain the utmost principles of the Dao,
changes in the five colors of the pulse,
measuring kuídù and assessing extraordinary conditions qíhéng—
the principle lies in unity.
The spirit transforms without reversing;
reversing leads to non-transformation,
thus losing its mechanism.
The essence of the utmost principles
is subtle and approaches closely.
Record it on a jade tablet
and call it 'Harmonizing the Jade Mechanism,' Hé Yù Jī."
15.2 The complexion shows indications in the upper, lower, left, and right aspects,
each located at its essential point.
If the color appears shallow,
decoctions are the primary treatment,
Ten days have passed.
For those whose symptoms appear deep-seated,
Qí Zhǔzhì (齊主治) should be the primary treatment,
twenty-one days and then stop.
For those whose symptoms appear very deep-seated,
Láojiǔ Zhǔzhì (醪酒主治) should be the primary treatment,
a hundred days and then stop.
If the complexion fades prematurely and the face loses its vitality,
do not treat.
A hundred days and it will all be over.
If the pulse is short and breath is cut off, death will occur.
If the disease is a warm disease and the deficiency is extreme, death will occur.
When coloration appears above, below, left, and right,
each is located at its essential position.
Above is considered rebellious,
below is considered compliant.
For women, the right is considered rebellious,
the left is considered compliant;
for men, the left is considered rebellious,
the right is considered compliant.
An excess of yang leads to death,
an excess of yin leads to death.
15.3 When yin and yang oppose each other,
the treatment lies in the struggle for equilibrium,
which is a matter of odd and even principles,
and a matter of assessing the situation.
Throbbing pulse with paralysis,
The intersection of cold and heat.
A solitary pulse indicates the depletion of *qì*;
diarrhea caused by deficiency indicates the loss of blood.
Solitary indicates opposition (rebellion);
deficiency indicates compliance (following).
Apply the methods of odd and even (extraordinary meridians),
starting with the *Tàiyīn*.
To proceed in a direction that it cannot overcome is called opposition;
opposition leads to death.
To proceed in a direction that it can overcome is called compliance;
compliance leads to life.
The dominance of the eight winds and the four seasons
ends and begins again.
If one travels in opposition even once,
it becomes uncountable (i.e., the damage is irreversible).
The essential discussion is complete.
Chapter Sixteen: The Essential Discussion of Diagnosis

In the first and second months,

Rén qì zài pí. [Human Qi resides in the spleen.]
Wǔ yuè liù yuè, [May and June,]

Up and down follow the same method;

Spring, summer, autumn, winter,

16.4 In general, when puncturing the chest and abdomen,

Puncturing to avoid the five viscera (wǔ zàng) requires

When puncturing the chest and abdomen,

If the puncture does not heal,
Repeated needling.

16.5 The Dì
said, "I wish to hear about the termination of the twelve meridians;
how is it?"
Qíbó
said, "The termination of the Tàiyáng
meridian is characterized by the eyes rolling upwards, the body bending backward and spasming,
its color being white,
and profuse sweating emerging;
once it emerges, one will die.
The termination of the Shǎoyáng

If the connecting tissues sever, death occurs within one and a half days.
At the time of death,
the complexion first turns bluish-white,
and then death occurs.
The termination of the Yángmíng
is characterized by the mouth and eyes moving involuntarily,
frequent fright, and nonsensical speech,
the complexion being yellow;
its upper and lower channels being full
and without sensation,
then it ends.
When Shǎoyīn (少陰) ends,
the face is black, the teeth are long and coated with grime,
the abdomen is distended and blocked,
the upper and lower parts are not communicating, and then it ends.
When Tàiyīn (太陰) ends,
the abdomen is distended and blocked, unable to breathe,
prone to belching and vomiting,
vomiting leads to counterflow,
counterflow leads to a red face,
if there is no counterflow, the upper and lower parts do not communicate,
if there is no communication, the face is black, and the skin and hair are scorched, and then it ends.
When Juéyīn (厥陰) ends,
there is heat in the middle, and the throat is dry,
prone to frequent urination and heart vexation,
severely, the tongue retracts, and the testicles draw upward, and then it ends.
These are the ways in which the twelve meridians are defeated.
*Mài Yào Jīng Wēi Lùn Piān* (脈要精微論篇, Discourse on the Essentials and Subtleties of the Pulse) Seventeenth
17.1 The Yellow Emperor (Huángdì, 黃帝) asked,
"What should be the method of diagnosis?"
Qíbó (岐伯) replied,
"The method of diagnosis should always be at daybreak,
when the *yīn* *qì* (陰氣) has not yet stirred,
the *yáng* *qì* (陽氣) has not yet dispersed,
food and drink have not yet been consumed,
the meridians have not yet flourished,
the network vessels are harmonized and even,
When the *qì* and blood are not yet disordered,
then it is possible to diagnose the pulse for indications of excesses.
By palpating the pulse's movement and stillness and observing the clarity of vision,
examining the five colors,
observing the excess or deficiency of the five *zàng* organs,
the strength or weakness of the six *fǔ* organs,
the flourishing or decline of the form,
one can use these factors to determine the boundary between life and death.
17.2 Indeed, the pulse
is the residence of the blood.
If it is long, the *qì* is well-regulated;
if it is short, the *qì* is diseased;
if it is rapid, there is mental vexation;
if it is large, the disease is progressing;
if it is excessively strong above, the *qì* rises too high;
if it is excessively strong below, the *qì* is distended;
if it is intermittent, the *qì* is declining;
if it is thin, the *qì* is deficient;
if it is hesitant (sè), there is heart pain;
when it comes in a surging, bounding (húnhún gézhì) manner like a gushing spring,
the disease progresses and the complexion deteriorates;
when it fades away gradually (miánmián) like a snapping string,
death. Indeed, clarity of vision and the five colors
are the outward manifestations of *qì*.
Red should be like vermilion wrapped in white,
not like ocher;
white should be like goose feathers,
It should not be like salt;
Blue should be like the luster of dark jade,
It should not be like indigo;
Yellow should be like realgar wrapped in silk,
It should not be like yellow earth;
Black should be like the color of heavy lacquer,
It should not be like dark earth.
When the subtle appearances of the five colors are manifested,
Its life will not be long.
Now, sharp eyesight
is used to see all things,
to distinguish white from black,
to discern short from long.
To take long for short,
to take white for black,
if this is so, then the eyesight is failing.
17.3 The five viscera
are the guardians of the center.
When the center is replete and full,
and the *qì* prevails over the fear of injury,
the voice is like speaking from inside a room.
This is the dampness of the central *qì*.
If one speaks softly,
and only speaks again after a whole day,
this is *qì* being depleted.
If one's clothes are not kept neat,
if one's speech is full of good and evil,
Not distinguishing between close and distant relatives
is a derangement of the spirit.
If granaries do not store (grain),
it is as if the doors and gates are left unfastened.
If water springs do not cease (flowing),
it is as if the bladder cannot retain (urine).
Those who maintain their guarding survive;
those who lose their guarding die.
Now, the five zàng organs
are the strength of the body.
The head is the residence of essence and clarity;
if the head is tilted and vision is deep-set,
the spirit will be taken away.
The back is the residence of the chest;
if the back is bent and the shoulders follow,
the residence will be ruined.
The waist is the residence of the kidneys;
if turning and shaking are not possible,
the kidneys will be exhausted.
The knees are the residence of the sinews;
if bending and extending are not possible,
and one stoops when walking,
the sinews will be exhausted.
The bones are the residence of the marrow;
if one cannot stand for long,
and trembles and shakes when walking,
the bones will be exhausted.
Obtaining strength leads to life;
To lose strength is to die.
17.4 Qíbó said:
To act contrary to the four seasons,
excess becomes essence,
deficiency becomes dissipation.
Responding with too much,
deficiency becomes essence;
responding with deficiency,
excess becomes dissipation.
When Yin and Yang do not correspond,
the disease is called obstruction (Guān Gé).
The Emperor said:
How do the pulses move with the four seasons?
How do I know the location of the disease?
How do I know the changes of the disease?
How do I know when the disease is sometimes internal?
How do I know when the disease is sometimes external?
I ask about these five things,
may I be allowed to hear about them?
Qíbó said:
Let me speak about its great connection with the revolving of the heavens.
Outside the myriad things,
within the six directions,
the changes of heaven and earth,
the responses of Yin and Yang,
the warmth of spring,
becomes the heat of summer,
The resentment of autumn
becomes the anger of winter.
The movement of these four changes
rises and falls with the pulse.
Spring corresponds to the compass,
summer corresponds to the square,
autumn corresponds to the balance,
winter corresponds to the weight.
Therefore, forty-five days after the winter solstice,
the *yáng qì* slightly rises,
and the *yīn qì* slightly falls.
Forty-five days after the summer solstice,
the *yīn qì* slightly rises,
and the *yáng qì* slightly falls.
*Yīn* and *yáng* have their times,
and set a limit with the pulse.
If the limit is reached and they are not in accordance,
then one knows the point where the pulse will separate.
The separation has a limit,
therefore one knows the time of death.
The subtlety lies in the pulse,
which must not be left unexamined.
Examining it requires discipline,
beginning with *yīn* and *yáng*.
The beginning has a process,
originating from the Five Elements.
The origination has a measure,
with the four seasons as its suitability.
Make sure to supplement what is missing.
Be as one with Heaven and Earth.
Grasp the essence of oneness,
so as to understand life and death.
Therefore, sounds correspond to the five tones,
colors correspond to the five elements,
and pulses correspond to *yīn* and *yáng*.
Thus, if *yīn* is excessive, one dreams of crossing great waters in fear;
if *yáng* is excessive, one dreams of great fires burning and scorching;
if both *yīn* and *yáng* are excessive, one dreams of mutual killing and destruction.
If the upper body is excessive, one dreams of flying;
if the lower body is excessive, one dreams of falling.
If one is very full, one dreams of giving;
if one is very hungry, one dreams of taking.
If the *gān* (liver) *qì* is excessive, one dreams of anger;
if the *fèi* (lung) *qì* is excessive, one dreams of weeping.
If there are many short worms, one dreams of gathering crowds;
if there are many long worms, one dreams of mutual fighting and destruction.
Therefore, holding the pulse has a way;
emptiness and stillness are the means of preservation.
The spring pulse is floating,
like a fish swimming in the waves.
The summer pulse is on the skin,
broad and ample, as if all things are abundant.
The autumn pulse is below the skin,
as hibernating insects are about to leave.
The winter pulse is in the bone,
as hibernating insects are hidden and secure,
A virtuous person dwells in a chamber.
Therefore it is said:
Those who know the internal, examine and record it;
those who know the external, end it and begin it.

Chapter 23: Xuānmíng Wǔ Qì Piān (宣明五氣篇)
23.1.1 What the Five Flavors Enter:
Sour enters the liver;
spicy enters the lungs;

23.1.2 What the Five Qì (氣) Cause to be Ill:
The heart manifests as hiccups;

the bladder being obstructed manifests as urinary retention;
lack of control manifests as involuntary urination;
the gallbladder manifests as anger;
This is called the five illnesses.
23.1.3 The confluence of the five essences:
When essence and Qi converge in the heart, there is joy;

when they converge in the spleen, there is fear;
when they converge in the kidneys, there is fright.
This is called the five convergences,
which occur when there is deficiency and mutual convergence.
23.1.4 The five organs' dislikes:

23.1.5 The five organs' transformation into fluids:

23.1.6 The five flavors' prohibitions:
Spicy (xīn) flavor courses through the Qi;

bone diseases should not consume too much bitter food;
sweet flavors travel to the flesh,
flesh diseases should not consume too much sweet food;
sour flavors travel to the sinews,
sinew diseases should not consume too much sour food;
these are called the five prohibitions,
do not allow excessive consumption.
23.1.7 The five disease manifestations:
Yīn diseases manifest in the bones,
Yáng diseases manifest in the blood,
Yīn diseases manifest in the flesh,
Yáng diseases manifest in the winter,
Yīn diseases manifest in the summer,
these are called the five manifestations.
23.1.8 The five evils that cause disorder:
If evil enters Yáng, it causes mania (kuáng),
if evil enters Yīn, it causes numbness (bì),
attacking Yáng causes *diān* disease (epilepsy/vertigo),
attacking Yīn causes muteness (yīn),
if Yáng enters into Yīn, it causes quiescence (jìng),
if Yīn emerges from Yáng, it causes anger (nù),
these are called the five disorders.
23.1.9 What the Five Evils Manifest:
If in spring, one obtains the autumn pulse;
if in summer, one obtains the winter pulse;
if in late summer, one obtains the spring pulse;
if in autumn, one obtains the summer pulse;
if in winter, one obtains the late summer pulse;
this is called "Yīn Emerging from Yáng";
the illness is characterized by frequent anger and is incurable;
this is what is meant by the Five Evils;
all lead to the same fate;
death is incurable.
23.1.10 What the Five Zàng Store:
The heart (xīn) stores the spirit (shén);
the lungs (fèi) store the corporeal soul (pò);
the liver (gān) stores the ethereal soul (hún);
the spleen (pí) stores intention (yì);
the kidneys (shèn) store will (zhì);
this is what is meant by what the Five Zàng store.
23.1.11 What the Five Zàng Govern:
The heart (xīn) governs the vessels (mài);
the lungs (fèi) govern the skin (pí);
the liver (gān) governs the tendons (jīn);
the spleen (pí) governs the flesh (ròu);
the kidneys (shèn) govern the bones (gǔ);
this is what is meant by what the Five Govern.
23.1.12 Injuries from the Five Labors:
Prolonged gazing injures the blood,
prolonged lying down injures the *qì*,
prolonged sitting injures the flesh,
prolonged standing injures the bones,
prolonged walking injures the tendons;
these are called the injuries from the Five Labors.
23.1.13 Correspondences of the Five Pulses:
The liver pulse is taut (*xián*),

the spleen pulse is intermittent (*dài*),
the lung pulse is superficial (*máo*),
the kidney pulse is stony (*shí*);
these are called the pulses of the five *zàng* organs.

the times of waxing and waning,

Tài Yīn Yáng Míng Lùn Piān (Treatise on Tài Yīn and Yáng Míng) Chapter Twenty-Nine
29.1 Huángdì asked:
Tài Yīn and Yáng Míng are exterior and interior,
The pulse of the spleen and stomach,
how are their illnesses different?
Qíbó replied:
The positions of yin and yang are different,

alternately rebellious and compliant,
sometimes following inward,
sometimes following outward,
the direction they follow is different,
therefore the diseases have different names.
The Emperor said:

Qíbó said:
Yang
is the qi of heaven,
governing the exterior;
yin
is the qi of earth,
governing the interior.
Therefore, the yang pathway is replete,
the yin pathway is deficient.
Therefore, those who are attacked by pathogenic wind and deficient evils,
yang receives it;
those whose eating and drinking are not regulated, and whose rising and resting are not timely,
yin receives it.
When yang receives it,
it enters the six fǔ organs;
when yin receives it,
Then it enters the five zàng organs.
It enters the six fǔ organs;
then the body becomes hot and one cannot sleep at regular times,
resulting in panting and gasping.
Entering the five zàng organs causes fullness and obstruction,
leading to diarrhea below,
and prolonged cases result in dysentery.
Therefore, the throat governs the qi of Heaven,
and the pharynx governs the qi of Earth.
Thus, yáng receives the qi of wind,
and yīn receives the qi of dampness.
Therefore, yīn qi ascends from the foot to the head,
and descends along the arm to the fingertips;
yáng qi ascends from the hand to the head,
and descends to the foot.
Therefore, it is said:
For yáng diseases,
they ascend to the extreme and then descend;
for yīn diseases,
they descend to the extreme and then ascend.
Therefore, those injured by wind
are first affected in the upper part of the body;
those injured by dampness
are first affected in the lower part of the body.
29.2.1 The Dì
said: "If the spleen is diseased, then the four limbs cannot be used,

The four limbs all receive their qi from the stomach,
but cannot reach the main channels.
They must depend on the spleen
to receive it.
Now, if the spleen is diseased and cannot transport the fluids of the stomach,
the four limbs cannot receive the qi of water and grain,
the qi will weaken day by day,
the pulse pathways will be obstructed,
and the tendons, bones, and muscles
will all have no qi to nourish them,
therefore they become useless.
29.2.2 The Emperor asked:

The spleen is earth,
governing the center.
It constantly nourishes the four viscera according to the four seasons.
Each viscera is entrusted with governance for eighteen days,
so it cannot govern a season independently.
The spleen stores
the essence of the stomach's earth.
Earth
generates all things and models itself after heaven and earth,
therefore, from top to bottom, to the head and feet,
it cannot govern a season.
29.2.3 The Emperor said:
"The spleen and stomach are connected only by a membrane,

Qíbó said:
"The Foot Taiyin is the Taiyin of the three Yin,

therefore the Taiyin circulates the Qi for the three Yin.
The Yangming
is the exterior,
the sea of the five viscera and six fu-organs,
and it also circulates the Qi for the three Yang.
The viscera and fu-organs each receive Qi from the Yangming according to their channels,
therefore it circulates the fluids for the stomach.
If the four limbs cannot receive the Qi from water and grains,
they will weaken day by day,
the Yin passages will be unfavorable,
and the sinews, bones, and muscles will have no Qi to generate,
therefore they cannot be used."

Chapter 31: Discussion on Febrile Diseases
31.1 The Yellow Emperor (Huángdì) asked:
"Now, all febrile diseases
belong to the category of *shānghán* (傷寒, cold damage).
