Chapter Sixty-eight: Great Treatise on the Six Subtle Meanings
68.1.1 The Yellow Emperor (Huáng Dì) asked, saying:
"Alas, how distant is
the Way of Heaven!
Like welcoming floating clouds,
or gazing into a deep abyss.
Gazing into a deep abyss is still measurable,
but welcoming floating clouds, one knows not their limit.
Teacher, you have often spoken of carefully adhering to the Way of Heaven.
I have heard and treasured it,
but secretly pondered its meaning,
not knowing what it refers to.
I wish that you, Teacher, would fully express your will and exhaustively explain this matter,
so that it will never be extinguished,"
lasting without end.
Can the Way of Heaven be learned?
Qí Bó, bowing his head and prostrating twice, replied:
"How insightful is your question about the Way of Heaven!
This is due to the sequence of Heaven and the times of waxing and waning."
68.1.2 The Emperor said:
"I wish to hear about the waxing and waning of the six sixes of the Heavenly Way."
Qí Bó said:
"Above and below have their positions,
left and right have their regulations.
Therefore, to the right of Shào Yáng,
Yáng Míng governs it.
To the right of Yáng Míng,
Tài Yáng governs it.
To the right of Tài Yáng,
Jué Yīn governs it.
To the right of Jué Yīn,
Shào Yīn governs it.
To the right of Shào Yīn,
Tài Yīn governs it.
To the right of Tài Yīn,
Shǎoyáng governs it.
This is what is meant by the manifestation of *qì*.
It means to face south and await it.
Therefore, it is said:
"According to the order of Heaven,
the times of flourishing and decline,
shifting light and fixing positions,
stand upright and await it."
This is what it means.
Above Shǎoyáng,
the *qì* of fire governs it,
within which is seen Juéyīn.
Above Yángmíng,
the *qì* of dryness governs it,
within which is seen Tàiyīn.
Above Tàiyáng,
the *qì* of cold governs it,
within which is seen Shǎoyīn.
Above Juéyīn,
the *qì* of wind governs it,
within which is seen Shǎoyáng.
Above Shǎoyīn,
the *qì* of heat governs it,
within which is seen Tàiyáng.
Above Tàiyīn,
the *qì* of dampness governs it,
within which is seen Yángmíng.
This is what is called the root.
[běn] (root) is below,
[zhōng] (center) is what is seen.
What is seen is below,
it is the manifestation of [qì] (vital energy).
The root and the manifestation are different,
the response of [qì] (vital energy) corresponds to different appearances.
68.1.3 The Emperor said:
There is that which arrives when it should,
there is that which arrives and does not arrive,
there is that which arrives and is excessive,
what is the reason for this?
Qíbó said:
That which arrives when it should is harmonious.
That which arrives and does not arrive,
is an insufficiency of the incoming [qì] (vital energy).
That which arrives before it should,
is an excess of the incoming [qì] (vital energy).
The Emperor said:
That which arrives and does not arrive,
that which arrives before it should,
what about them?
Qíbó said:
To correspond is to accord,
not to correspond is to oppose.
To oppose, then changes arise;
when changes arise, then there is illness.
The Emperor said:
Good. Please tell me its correspondence.
Qí Bó said:
Things correspond to their birth.
Qi corresponds to the pulse.
68.2.1 The Emperor said:
Good. I would like to hear how the geographical correspondence relates to the six seasonal qi positions.
Qí Bó said:
To the right of Xiǎnmíng,
is the position of the Sovereign Fire.
To the right of the Sovereign Fire,
receding one step,
the Minister Fire governs it.
Advancing one step again,
the Earth Qi governs it.
Advancing one step again,
the Metal Qi governs it.
Advancing one step again,
the Water Qi governs it.
Advancing one step again,
the Wood Qi governs it.
Advancing one step again,
the Sovereign Fire governs it.
Below the Minister Fire,
the Water Qi supports it.
Below the Water position,
the Earth Qi supports it.
Below the Earth position,
the Wind Qi supports it.
Below the Wind position,
the Metal Qi supports it.
Below the Metal position,
the Fire Qi supports it.
Below the Sovereign Fire,
the *yīn jīng* (yin essence) receives it.
The Emperor said:

Qíbó said:
When it is excessive, it causes harm.

When it controls, it produces transformation.
Outwardly, it manifests flourishing and decline.
When it causes harm, it brings failure and disorder.
Production and transformation prevent major illnesses.
68.2.2 The Emperor said:

When it is not in its proper position, it is perverse.

When the wood transport arrives at *mǎo*,
When the Fire phase arrives, it corresponds to *wǔ* 午;

when the Metal phase arrives, it corresponds to *yǒu* 酉;
when the Water phase arrives, it corresponds to *zǐ* 子;

The Emperor said:

The year does not correspond with the *huì* 會.

In a year of the Earth phase,

in a year of the Water phase,

What about this?
Qíbó 歧伯 said:
This is the *huì* 會 of the Heaven.

*Tiān Fú* 天符.
What about *Tiān Fú Suì Huì* 天符歲會?
Qíbó 歧伯 said:
This concerns the convergence of Tài Yī and Tiān Fú.
The Emperor said:

When the executor of commands is struck,

The Emperor said:

Qíbó said:

With rebellion, the disease is near

With obedience, the disease is distant
and the harm is subtle.
This is what is called 'two fires.'"

Shàn. Yuàn wén qí bù héfūrú.

What is meant by "progresses" is that

The Emperor said:

Positions have beginnings and endings,

Heavenly *qì* begins with *jiǎ*,

Carefully observe their times,

The *sì zhī qì* (fourth phase) begins at thirty-seven and six-tenths *kè*,

The *wǔ zhī qì* (fifth phase) begins at twenty-six *kè*,

The *liù zhī qì* (sixth phase) begins at twelve and six-tenths *kè*,

This is the count of Heaven.
In the year *wù chén*,

The Emperor said:

the middle,

The Yellow Emperor said:

Qíbó said:
"Ascending and then descending,

Descending and then ascending,
the ascending is called Earth.
Heaven's Qi descends,
Qi flows to the Earth;
Earth's Qi ascends,
Qi rises to Heaven.
Therefore, high and low summon each other,
ascent and descent depend on each other,
and transformations arise."
68.4.2 The Emperor said:
"Excellent. Cold and dampness meet in the ditches,

"The Qi has dominance and recovery,
the occurrence of dominance and recovery,
has virtue and transformation,
has use and change,
change then allows evil Qi to reside there."
The Emperor said:
"What is meant by evil?"
Qíbó said:
"The birth of things follows transformation,
the extreme of things is due to change,
the mutual impact of transformation and change,
is the reason for success and failure.
Therefore, the Qi has going and returning,
use has slowness and speed,
the four have being, and transform, and change,
is the coming of wind."
The Emperor said:
"Slowness and speed, going and returning,

and transform and change,
therefore it depends on the changes of flourishing and decline.
Success and failure rely on each other and lie hidden in the middle,
Why is that?
Qíbó said:
Success and failure, reliance and concealment, arise from movement.
If movement does not cease,
then changes will occur.
The Yellow Emperor said:
Is there a fixed period?
Qíbó said:
Without production and transformation,
that is the period of stillness.
The Yellow Emperor said:
Is there no production and transformation?
Qíbó said:
If outflow and inflow are abandoned, then the divine mechanism of transformation will be extinguished.
If ascending and descending cease, then the vital energy will stand alone and in danger.
Therefore, without outflow and inflow,
there is no way for birth, growth, maturity, and aging to cease.
Without ascending and descending,
there is no way for birth, growth, transformation, and storage to occur.
Therefore, ascending, descending, outflow, and inflow
are present in all vessels.
Thus, the vessel is the abode of production and transformation.
If the vessel disperses, then it separates,
and production and transformation cease.
Therefore, there is nothing without outflow and inflow,
and nothing without ascending and descending.
Transformations have small and large degrees,
and periods have near and far durations.
Those who possess these four qualities value constant adherence to them;
acting contrary to the norm will bring calamity.
Therefore, it is said, "Without form, without worry,"
this is what it means.
The Emperor said:
Good. Is there anything that does not generate or transform?
Qíbó said:
How thorough your question is!
Only the True Person
is in harmony with the Dao.
The Emperor said:
Good.

71.1.8.4 The Emperor said:

Qíbó said:
"Do not treat heat with heat,

Following it brings harmony;
opposing it brings illness.
One must not fail to respect and fear them and stay away from them;
this is what is meant by the arising of the six positions with the seasons."
The Emperor said:
How should one consider warmth and coolness?
Qíbó said:
When the dominant *qì* is heat,
use heat without transgression.
When the dominant *qì* is cold,
use cold without transgression.
When the dominant *qì* is coolness,
use coolness without transgression.
When the dominant *qì* is warmth,
use warmth without transgression.
When the intervening *qì* is the same as the dominant *qì*, there is no transgression.
When it is different from the dominant *qì*, then there is a minor transgression.
This is called the "Four Fears,"
and must be carefully observed.
The Emperor said:
Good. What happens when one transgresses?
Qíbó said:
When the weather is contrary to the season,
then one can follow the season.
And when it overcomes its master, then it can be transgressed,
with the aim of achieving balance,
but it should not be exceeded.
This is called "evil *qì* rebelling and overcoming."
Therefore, it is said:
Do not lose faith in the heavens,
do not go against the suitability of *qì*,
do not aid its dominance,
No one praises its restoration;
this is called supreme governance.

74.2.5 The Emperor said:
What is the reversion of the six qì?
Qíbó (岐伯) said:
How thorough your question!
The reversion of Juéyīn (厥陰) manifests as
hardness and fullness in the lower abdomen,
urgency and sudden pain internally,
fallen trees and flying sand,
naked insects not thriving,
pain in the Jueyin heart meridian,
sweating, vomiting,
food and drink not entering,
entering and then exiting again,
trembling and dizziness of the tendons and bones,
cold reversal,
and, in severe cases, entering the spleen,
causing food bi syndrome with vomiting.
If the Chōngyáng (衝陽) pulse is severed,
death is certain and untreatable.
The reversion of Shàoyīn (少陰) manifests as
smoldering heat arising internally,
irritability, nasal congestion, and sneezing,
gripping pain in the lower abdomen,
fire seen burning and scorching, and dryness in the throat.
Urine is excreted in spurts, stopping intermittently,
Qi (氣) movement originates from the left,
Ascending towards the right,
Causing coughing and pain in the skin,
Sudden loss of voice, heart pain, mental confusion, disorientation, and being unaware of one's surroundings.
Then comes shivering, aversion to cold, trembling, delirium, and incoherent speech.
After the cold subsides, heat arises,
Causing thirst and a desire to drink.
Shortness of breath, weakness of the bones, abdominal distention, and constipation occur.
Externally, there is generalized edema, hiccupping, and belching.
Reddish Qi (氣) manifests later,
Water flows but does not freeze,
Hot Qi (氣) extensively prevails,
Shellfish and insects do not reappear,
Diseases include miliaria, rashes, sores, carbuncles, furuncles, acne, and hemorrhoids,
Severely, it can penetrate the lungs,
Causing coughing and nasal discharge.
When the Tiānfǔ (天府) point is cut off,
Death is certain and untreatable.
When the Tàiyīn (太陰) stage reverts,
Dampness transformations then manifest,
Causing heaviness of the body and fullness in the middle abdomen,
Food and drink not transforming,
*yīn* *qì* rising upwards,
discomfort in the chest,
drink accumulating in the middle burner,
coughing and panting with sound,
heavy rain occurring frequently,
scales seen on land,
severe headache with heaviness,
and tremors and convulsions especially severe,
vomiting, and constantly silently spitting clear liquid,
severely affecting the kidneys,
causing uncontrolled discharge from the orifices.
If *Tài Xī* (太谿) pulse is severed,
death is untreatable.
When *shǎo yáng* (少陽) recovers,
great heat will arrive,
dryness and scorching burning,
Jiè chóng nǎi hào,
alarming convulsions and cough with blood,
heart heat and irritability,
frequent bowel movements and aversion to wind,
counterflow of qi upwards,
face like floating dust,
eyes twitching and convulsive,
internal fire energy erupting,
manifesting as oral thrush and vomiting upwards,
blood overflowing and blood flowing out,
developing into malaria,
chills and shivering,
extreme cold turning to heat,
throat passages scorched and withered,
thirst driving one to drink water,
complexion changing to yellow and red,
shortness of breath and weak pulse,
transforming into fluid retention,
spreading to cause edema,
severely entering the lungs,
causing coughing with blood.
If the Chǐzé point is severed,
death is certain and untreatable.
The recovery of Yángmíng,
the great rise of clear qi,
dense forests and flourishing trunks,
furred creatures then become rampant,
illness arises in the hypochondria,
When *qì* returns to the left,
one is prone to sighing.
Severely, it causes heart pain and fullness,
abdominal distention and diarrhea,
bitter vomiting, coughing, hiccupping, and vexation of the heart.
The disease is in the diaphragm, causing headaches.
Severely, it enters the liver,
causing fright, shock, and muscle spasms.
If Tàichōng (太衝) is severed,
death will occur and the condition will be incurable.
The return of the Tàiyáng (太陽):
rebellious *qì* ascends,
water condenses into rain and ice,
and feathered creatures die.
Cold is generated in the heart and stomach,
the chest and diaphragm become dysfunctional,
resulting in heart pain and fullness,
headaches and frequent sadness,
occasional dizziness and fainting.
Appetite decreases, and the waist and buttocks experience referred pain,
making bending and stretching difficult.
The ground cracks and the ice hardens,
and sunlight cannot cure the condition.
The lower abdomen pulls on the testicles,
drawing the lumbar spine upwards, assaulting the heart,
with the spitting out of clear fluids, and hiccupping and belching resulting.
Severely, it enters the heart,
causing frequent forgetfulness and sadness.
If Shénmén (神門) is severed,
death will occur and the condition will be incurable.
The Emperor said:
Good. How should it be treated?
